# Comparisons

This folder contains detailed comparative analyses of clinical quality indicators, patient demographics, and treatment outcomes for atrial fibrillation (atrieflimren) in Denmark, as tracked by the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDK). The pages evaluate regional and national performance against established healthcare standards, covering metrics such as anticoagulation initiation times, echocardiography and TSH testing rates, long-term medication adherence, and the incidence of severe complications like ischemic stroke, intracranial hemorrhage, and heart failure. Additionally, it includes breakdowns of patient risk profiles using the CHA2DS2-VASc score, comparisons of bleeding risks across different anticoagulant therapies (DOACs vs. Marevan), and reference tables for the specific diagnostic and procedural codes used in the registry's data collection.

## Pages

- [[alder-ved-diagnose-for-incidente-patienter|Alder ved diagnose for incidente patienter]] — Compares the average, median, and extreme ages at diagnosis for newly identified atrial fibrillation patients across Danish regions.
- [[alder-ved-diagnose|Alder ved diagnose]] — Analyzes the age distribution at diagnosis for atrial fibrillation patients, highlighting regional uniformities and outliers in minimum and maximum ages.
